question: Your team adds a pipeline step that starts Claude Code with a pull request review prompt, in the same way that developers start it on their own machines. The step never finishes, and the CI system kills the job only when it reaches its time limit. The logs show that Claude Code is waiting for interactive input. What is the most effective way to fix this pipeline step?

options.text: Increase the time limit of the CI job so Claude Code has enough time to complete the review before the job is killed.
options.reason: The step hangs because Claude Code waits for interactive input; a longer time limit only delays the failure, while the guide says non-interactive mode with the --print flag prevents the hang.

options.text: Add the --print flag to the invocation so Claude Code processes the prompt, prints its result, and exits without waiting for input.
options.reason: The guide names the --print flag as the way to run Claude Code in non-interactive mode in automated pipelines, which prevents interactive input hangs.

options.text: Add the --output-format json flag to the invocation so the pipeline receives machine-parseable output without any user interaction.
options.reason: The guide describes --output-format json as a way to enforce structured output in CI; it does not switch Claude Code to non-interactive mode, so the hang remains.

options.text: Add a rule to the project CLAUDE.md file that tells Claude Code to finish every review without asking the user any questions.
options.reason: The guide describes CLAUDE.md as the way to give project context such as review criteria; it does not change the execution mode, so the session still waits for input.
